findings.evidence: copier.yml:21 validator is `{% if not ci_runner_labels | trim %}...`. The template renders `'[' ~ runner_labels | join(', ') ~ ']'` with no validation. The spec scenario 'Invalid self-hosted labels' says `rendering or platform_doctor fails`, and the render test covers only blank labels (tests/test_ci_runner_selection.py:533-537). Moving the grammar check into the validator would fail at the source.
findings.summary: The Copier validator only rejects an empty `ci_runner_labels` value. The label grammar (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`, no empty entries, no duplicates) is enforced only later by `platform_doctor`. Rendering therefore accepts labels such as `a,,b`, `a b`, `a]` or `a,a` and writes them into `runs-on` unescaped. The malformed workflow is committed and only fails when the doctor runs.

findings.evidence: template dev-platform.yml.jinja line `runs-on: {{ ... runner_labels[0] ... }}`. CI_RUNNER_LABEL_RE in platform_doctor.py allows `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`. The tests only use `alters`, `a` and `self-hosted,linux`.
findings.summary: A single label is rendered as a bare YAML scalar. Labels the grammar allows can parse as non-strings: `true`, `null`, `1.5` and `on` become bool, null or number, and `-` is a sequence indicator. The doctor compares raw text, so it would not catch this. Multi-label lists have the same issue per element.
